newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed in thin trade.

text.p: Leading shares closed mixed on Monday in quiet and thin trading after last week's delay in disbursing the latest tranche of the International Monetary Fund loan and the dilution of Surgutneftegaz shares, traders said.
They said they expected prices to fluctuate in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 companies fell 1.65 percent to 176.52 on $13.50 million in volume.

"This is a continuation of last week's trend," said Oleg Tatkov, a trader from Renaissance Capital. "After a plunge the fall slowed down a bit. But the news about the tranche delay is still the biggest news."

Last week an IMF mission left Moscow without agreeing to pay the next tranche of its $10 billion loan, largely because it is concerned about Russia's poor tax collection performance. The mission will return in the second half of November for more talks.
Tatkov said the market had already absorbed the news about Surgut Holding acquiring the whole of Surgutneftegaz's new issue.
He said that although the negative mood would continue, the share would no longer fall heavily.
Surgutneftegaz Holding said last week it had acquired a new issue of shares in its partly owned Surgutneftegaz unit to boost control over the company.
Surgutneftegaz ordinaries traded at $0.395 after $0.396 at Friday's close.

The recent Gazprom American Depositary Share issue has siphoned off funds from the Russian market, while Western investors shifted their money into second-tier shares, said Alexander Bobolev, a broker from IK Aton.
"These reasons very much account for the fall in blue chips," he said.
News the government planned to look into whether Varyoganneftegaz, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz and Noyabrskneftegaz had paid all their taxes deterred some investors from buying the stock, Bobolev said.
"Of course, the news made a negative impact on the people who wanted to buy those shares, but it created no panic, as the market in these shares is underdeveloped," he said.
Noyabrskneftegaz rose to $5.16 from $5.12 at Thursday's close, when it was last traded. Nizhnevartovskneftegaz and Varyoganneftegaz were not traded.
But Bobolev said the deal was not indicative.
Gazprom was the loss leader of the day with prices falling following a slip in ADS prices on the London exchange, Bobolev said.

Gazprom fell to $0.43 from $0.51, Sverdlovskenergo edged up to $0.250 from $0.225, UES was $0.0800 after $0.0809, Mosenergo fell to $0.94 from $0.95 and Novosibirskenergo rose to $1.9 from 1.7 on October 11, when it was last traded.
